correctness.rationale: The update is invertible. For adjacency, with coordinates (root a, nonroot vector b, leaf c), the sum-zero subspace of b has dimension n−2 and eigenvalue −1. The cubic factor is obtained from the induced map on (a,Σb,c), and when n−1 is nonzero it also acts on the three-dimensional complementary constant sector. Its temporal polynomial is z³g_n(z+z⁻¹); in residue 0 the stated sextic divides Φ28 modulo 3 and is square-free, and in residue 2 the product (z²+1)(z⁴+1) consists of distinct roots of orders four and eight as claimed. In residue 1, for B=A+I the displayed coordinate equations give rank(B)=3 and rank(B²)=2 on the n+1 dimensional space; the algebraic multiplicity of adjacency −1 is n. Accordingly one length-three block and n−3 length-one blocks are the only possibilities there, plus the simple +1 block. On an adjacency Jordan block of length j at −1, the companion pencil reduces to (z−1)²I−zN. Its (j−1)-minor on the superdiagonal is a unit at z=1; its determinant is (z−1)^(2j). Hence there is one length-2j temporal block, not two length-j blocks. The +1 adjacency block gives a length-two block at temporal −1. On a unipotent block, writing k=3^a b with 3∤b reduces the fixed dimension to the kernel of the 3^a-th power of its nilpotent part, since the remaining factor is a unit. The negative block contributes only for even k. This proves all dimensions, and a cyclic vector in each relevant block realizes the indicated least common multiple. Ranks are unchanged on extension fields and the number of states in a kernel of dimension d is q^d; division by the primitive period after Möbius inversion counts orbits rather than states. For the intact clique, J²=nJ gives one length-two adjacency block at −1 if 3|n; otherwise decompose into the line of constants and the sum-zero subspace, yielding 9/12/6 in the respective classes. All required primary types occur for the permitted smallest sizes.
